title: Space-valued straightening and the ordinary-base adjoint comparison
statement:
Use simplicial sets, Kan complexes, quasicategories, internal functor simplicial sets and weak homotopy equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], left fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$. For clarity the coherent-nerve notation used here is defined as follows. A simplicial category $A$ has simplicial mapping sets and associative unital simplicial composition. Let $Q_r$ have objects $0,\ldots,r$, mapping simplicial set $N(P_{ij})$ for $i\leq j$, where $P_{ij}$ is the inclusion poset of subsets of $\{i,\ldots,j\}$ containing both endpoints, and empty mapping set for $i>j$; composition is union of subsets. Put $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(A)_r=\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{sCat}}(Q_r,A)$, with operators induced by images of subsets under monotone maps. For a strict diagram of Kan complexes, its coherent functor is the nerve of the simplicial functor from the discrete simplicial category $C$. Let $\mathsf{Kan}_{\mathcal U}$ be the simplicial category of small Kan complexes with mapping simplicial sets $\operatorname{Fun}(K,L)$, and put $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathsf{Kan}_{\mathcal U})$. For a small quasicategory $B$, let $\mathsf L_B$ be the simplicial category of small left fibrations over $B$, whose mapping $n$-simplices from $E$ to $E'$ are maps $E\times\Delta^n\to E'$ over $B$. Its mapping simplicial sets are Kan. There is an equivalence
$$\operatorname{St}_B:N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathsf L_B)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}),$$
natural under base pullback and precomposition. A left fibration is classified by $G:B\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ when its image under this equivalence is equivalent to $G$.

Here is the comparison for an arbitrary small ordinary category $C$, with no Kan assumption on diagrams in the adjunction. For $\sigma:[r]\to C$ define a diagram $A_\sigma:C\to\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathcal U}$. At $c$, it is the degreewise quotient
$$A_\sigma(c)=\left(\coprod_{\varnothing\ne J\subseteq[r]}\Delta^J\times\operatorname{Hom}_C(\sigma(\max J),c)\right)/\sim,$$
where $\Delta^J=N(J)$, each hom set is discrete, and for $\varnothing\ne I\subseteq J$, $z\in(\Delta^I)_m$ and $h:\sigma(\max J)\to c$ the relation identifies $(J,\iota_{IJ}z,h)$ with $(I,z,h\circ\sigma(\max I\to\max J))$. The action on $c$ is postcomposition of $h$. A monotone $\theta:[s]\to[r]$ induces $A_{\sigma\theta}\to A_\sigma$ by $(J,z,h)\mapsto(\theta(J),\Delta(\theta|_J)z,h)$. For any simplicial map $X\to N(C)$ define
$$L_C(X)=\operatorname{colim}_{(\Delta^r\xrightarrow{x}X)}A_{p x}$$
in strict $C$-diagrams of simplicial sets; this is the colimit over the category of simplices of $X$. The functor $L_C$ admits a right adjoint $R_C$, characterized by natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathsf{sSet}/N(C)}(X,R_C G)\cong\operatorname{Nat}_C(L_C(X),G).$$
For every strict Kan-valued diagram $G:C\to\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathcal U}$, the adjunction counit
$$\epsilon_G:L_C(R_CG)\longrightarrow G$$
is an objectwise weak homotopy equivalence. For every small left fibration $p:X\to N(C)$, the diagram $L_C(X)$ represents $\operatorname{St}_{N(C)}(p)$: more precisely, if $L_C(X)\to D$ is an objectwise weak homotopy equivalence into a strict Kan-valued diagram, then $\operatorname{St}_{N(C)}(p)\simeq N_{\mathrm{hc}}(D)$. Here $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(D):N(C)\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ is induced by the simplicial functor from the discrete simplicial category $C$ which is constant on each mapping set at the corresponding strict diagram map. These statements are natural in $X$ and $G$; they do not require projective cofibrancy of $G$.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.1.2 (covariant dual) and Section 3.3.2 (classification); Remark 3.2.5.5 (relative-nerve left adjoint), Remark 3.2.5.10 and Lemma 3.2.5.17(1) (natural straightening comparison on every X), Proposition 3.2.5.18(1) (Quillen equivalence and counit for fibrant diagrams). The displayed A_sigma quotient spells out the left adjoint on simplices. Read online, not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: Use [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] and [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] for the locally Kan model and space conventions. The replacement formulas and pullback compatibility supplied by [lem-coef-covariant-derived-replacement-base-change], together with the localization comparison of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization], define the normalized derived equivalence. The enriched evaluation comparison of [lem-coef-enriched-diagram-rectification] identifies its value on an objectwise Kan diagram with the coherent nerve of that diagram, including all coherences. For objectwise Kan input, its trivial-fibration cofibrant replacement remains fibrant and has the same localized enriched evaluation by that replacement lemma.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.1.2, covariant dual; Proposition 4.2.4.4 and Section 3.3.2.

proof.text: Here is a degreewise description of the given colimit. For an $m$-simplex $z$ of $\Delta^J$, represented by $\alpha:[m]\to J$, the quotient relation replaces $(J,z,h)$ by its representative with $I=\operatorname{im}\alpha$ and arrow $h\sigma(\alpha(m)\to\max J)$. Therefore $(A_\sigma(c))_m$ consists exactly of pairs $(\alpha:[m]\to[r],h:\sigma(\alpha(m))\to c)$. The invariant pair just written also shows that two reduced representatives agree only when these pairs agree. On passing to the colimit over simplices of $X$, the pairs become $(x\in X_m,h:p(x(m))\to c)$. Thus, naturally in $X,c$, $L_C(X)(c)=X\times_{N(C)}N(C/c)$, where $C/c$ has objects arrows $d\to c$ and arrows commuting triangles, and maps to $C$ by their sources. In this formula $d_i(x,h)=(d_i x,h)$ for $i<m$, while $d_m(x,h)=(d_mx,h\,p(x(m-1)\to x(m)))$; degeneracies duplicate the corresponding vertex. These formulas also verify the specified maps of $A_\sigma$ under every monotone map, including degeneracies. The simplex category is small since its objects and arrows are unions of sets indexed by the natural numbers.

source.place: Remark 3.2.5.5 and Example 3.2.5.6; explicit calculation of the quotient and simplex colimit.

proof.text: For any strict simplicial-set-valued diagram $G$, define $(R_CG)_r$ over $\sigma:[r]\to C$ to consist of maps $t_J:\Delta^J\to G(\sigma(\max J))$ for all nonempty $J\subseteq[r]$, with $t_J|_{\Delta^I}=G(\sigma(\max I)\to\sigma(\max J))t_I$. Operators are $t'_J=t_{\theta(J)}\Delta(\theta|_J)$ over $\sigma\theta$. They compose because images of subsets and restrictions compose, so this defines a simplicial set over $N(C)$. A natural transformation $A_\sigma\to G$ gives $t_J$ by evaluating on the summand with $c=\sigma(\max J)$ and $h=\mathrm{id}$; conversely $t_J$ defines its value on $(J,z,h)$ as $G(h)t_J(z)$. The quotient relations are exactly the displayed compatibility. The colimit universal property consequently identifies natural maps $L_C(X)\to G$ with compatible choices of these data for every simplex of $X$, namely maps $X\to R_CG$ over $N(C)$. Both constructions are inverse and commute with precomposition and postcomposition. This proves the adjunction without a Kan assumption.

source.place: Definition 3.2.5.2 and Remark 3.2.5.5; explicit adjunction on simplices.

proof.text: In the pullback formula of step 2, the counit at $c$ sends $(\sigma,(t_J),h:\sigma(m)\to c)$ to $G(h)t_{[m]}\in G(c)_m$. Its section $s_c$ sends a simplex of $G(c)$ to the constant base string at $c$, with arrow $\mathrm{id}_c$ and all $t_J$ given by restrictions of that simplex. Here is a simplicial homotopy from the identity to $s_c\epsilon_{G,c}$. Given also $\beta:[m]\to[1]$, replace the vertex $d_i=\sigma(i)$ by $c$ exactly when $\beta(i)=1$; the mixed arrows are $h_i=h\sigma(i\to m)$, and arrows between replaced vertices are identities. Replace $t_J$ by $t_J$ when $\beta(\max J)=0$ and by $G(h_{\max J})t_J$ otherwise; the new final arrow is $h$ or $\mathrm{id}_c$ accordingly. The relations hold because $h_j\sigma(i\to j)=h_i$, and restriction along every monotone map preserves these formulas. At endpoints this is respectively the identity and $s_c\epsilon_{G,c}$, and $\epsilon_{G,c}s_c=\mathrm{id}$. A simplicial homotopy equivalence induces inverse maps on edge components of every internal functor set into a Kan complex, by precomposing with the homotopies. The criterion of [lem-cbc-realization-weak-equivalence] therefore makes $\epsilon_{G,c}$ a weak homotopy equivalence. This proof even works for arbitrary $G$; in particular it proves the required Kan-valued case without projective cofibrancy.

source.place: Remark 3.2.5.5, Example 3.2.5.6 and Proposition 3.2.5.18(1); explicit comma-category contraction in place of the Quillen counit criterion.

proof.text: Let $X\to N(C)$ now be a left fibration. Fix $c$ and set $E=X\times_{N(C)}N(C/c)=L_C(X)(c)$. Its map to $N(C/c)$ is a left fibration: every horn lifting problem projects to the given left-fibration lifting problem in $X$ and a filler pairs with its already specified base simplex. The ordinary category $C/c$ has terminal object $\mathrm{id}_c$. The unique arrows to it define $b:N(C/c)\times\Delta^1\to N(C/c)$ from the identity to its constant map; this is constant on the terminal vertex. Apply [lem-coef-left-fibration-relative-cylinder-lifting] with $K=E$, $A=X_c\subset E$, base homotopy $b(p_E(-),-)$, initial map $\mathrm{id}_E$, and the constant homotopy on $X_c$. The endpoint of the resulting lift lands in $X_c$ and gives $r:E\to X_c$ with $r i_c=\mathrm{id}$ and $i_c r$ simplicially homotopic to $\mathrm{id}_E$. As in step 4, [lem-cbc-realization-weak-equivalence] implies that $i_c:X_c\to L_C(X)(c)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. No choice of these contractions natural in $c$ is claimed or needed.

source.place: Corollaries 2.1.2.7 and 2.1.2.10; terminal-object contraction of C/c, as used in Remark 3.2.5.5.

proof.text: For a strict Kan-valued diagram $D$, the explicit $R_CD$ of step 3 is a left fibration. Indeed a left horn over $\sigma:[r]\to C$, missing face $i<r$, already specifies $t_J$ for all subsets except $[r]$ and $[r]\setminus\{i\}$. Transport the face data into $D(\sigma(r))$. They give a horn there, which has a filler since it is Kan. Use that filler for $t_{[r]}$ and its missing face for $t_{[r]\setminus\{i\}}$. All remaining relations are the prescribed horn relations; this also covers $r=1,i=0$. Its fiber at $c$ is $D(c)$, since the full-set map determines all others over a constant base string. The transport is precisely the strict diagram transport: for each base simplex $\sigma:[r]\to C$ the map $\Delta^r\times D(\sigma(0))\to R_CD$ sends an $m$-simplex $(\alpha:[m]\to[r],y)$ to $\sigma\alpha$ and $t_J=D(\sigma(0)\to\sigma(\alpha(\max J)))\,y|_{\Delta^J}$. Restrictions not removing the initial vertex agree literally, while restriction starting at a later vertex agrees after applying the strict map $D(\sigma(0)\to\sigma(k))$ to the input. Hence these maps retain exactly the strict composition and unit coherences. This calculation proves the left-fibration and fiber assertions only. The identification of its coherent classifying functor will instead follow from the concrete-construction comparison in steps 7–9, applied to the counit of step 4.

source.place: Definition 3.2.5.2 and the direct horn argument behind Corollary 3.2.5.19; strict transport identified as in Proposition 3.2.5.21.

proof.text: For $p:X\to N(C)$ set $B=N(C)$ and $S=B^{\mathrm{op}}$. Let $\phi:\mathfrak C[S]\to C^{\mathrm{op}}$ be the counit and put $H_C(X)=L_\phi(X^{\mathrm{op}})$, using exactly the ordered-cone pushout of [lem-coef-unmarked-straightening-quillen]. The existing concrete-construction comparison [lem-coef-unmarked-relative-nerve-cone-comparison] gives the natural objectwise weak homotopy equivalence $\alpha_{C,X}:H_C(X)\to F_C(X)^{\mathrm{op}}$, with $F_C(X)(c)=X\times_{N(C)}N(C/c)$. This is the same $L_C(X)$ calculated in step 2, not a new classifying-functor assertion. Its map on the universal simplex is induced by the nerve of $J\mapsto\min J$ on the subset cube, descending through the cone-pushout relations into the opposite ordered interval; left Kan extension and simplex colimits specify it on every input. In particular it applies to a left fibration $X$ without imposing any additional cofibrancy condition.

source.place: Remark 3.2.5.10 and Lemma 3.2.5.17(1), unmarked concrete-construction comparison.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-unmarked-cone-model-comparison] to the given $v:L_C(X)\to D$. Its hypotheses give the Dwyer--Kan counit, cofibrancy of the ordered-cone diagram, the natural identification $u_!P\cong H_C(X)$, and the weak equivalence of the enriched Kan-extension adjoint. The explicit comparison map $\alpha_{C,X}$ is the one in [lem-coef-unmarked-relative-nerve-cone-comparison]; since opposite preserves weak homotopy equivalences by [lem-coef-infinity-opposite-subdivision-kan-zigzag] (natural homeomorphism $|T^{\mathrm{op}}|\cong|T|$), $v^{\mathrm{op}}$ and hence $w=v^{\mathrm{op}}\alpha_{C,X}$ are objectwise weak; $D^{\mathrm{op}}$ is objectwise Kan by the same node. The cone criterion then identifies $\operatorname{St}_{N(C)}(X)$ with enriched evaluation on $u^*D^{\mathrm{op}}$, and [lem-coef-enriched-diagram-rectification] identifies this evaluation on every $Q_r$ with $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(D^{\mathrm{op}})$.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.1.2; Lemma 3.2.5.17(1); Proposition 4.2.4.4; Proposition A.3.3.8. Derived cone/left-Kan-extension and enriched-evaluation calculation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-opposite-subdivision-kan-zigzag] to every value $T=D(c)$. Its zigzag $T\to ET\leftarrow E\operatorname{Sd}T\to E(T^{\mathrm{op}})\leftarrow T^{\mathrm{op}}$ consists of Kan complexes and weak homotopy equivalences and is natural in $T$, so it commutes with every strict map $D(c\to c')$ and gives a strict zigzag of objectwise weak equivalences of strict Kan-valued $C$-diagrams $D\to ED\leftarrow E\operatorname{Sd}D\to E(D^{\mathrm{op}})\leftarrow D^{\mathrm{op}}$, natural in $D$. $\operatorname{Sd}$ and $E=\operatorname{Ex}^\infty$ keep $\mathcal U$-small inputs $\mathcal U$-small, so every term lies in $\mathsf{Kan}_{\mathcal U}$. A strict transformation is a simplicial functor $C\times[1]\to\mathsf{Kan}_{\mathcal U}$, and its coherent nerve is a transformation $N(C)\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ whose component at $c$ is the edge given by the weak equivalence at $c$. A weak homotopy equivalence of Kan complexes, a weak equivalence between bifibrant objects of the Kan model structure, is an equivalence in $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ by [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. The pointwise criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes each of the four transformations an equivalence in $\operatorname{Fun}(N(C),\mathcal S_{\mathcal U})$. Hence $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(D^{\mathrm{op}})\simeq N_{\mathrm{hc}}(D)$, naturally in $D$; composing with step 8 removes the valuewise opposite and gives $\operatorname{St}_{N(C)}(p)\simeq N_{\mathrm{hc}}(D)$.

source.place: Opposite normalization of the space-valued comparison (HTT Lemma 3.2.5.17(1) yields the valuewise opposite); natural Kan zigzag between a Kan complex and its opposite, and the pointwise equivalence criterion.

proof.text: In particular apply steps 7–9 to $X=R_CD$ (a left fibration by step 6) and $v=\epsilon_D$ (objectwise a weak equivalence by step 4). This now proves $\operatorname{St}_{N(C)}(R_CD)\simeq N_{\mathrm{hc}}(D)$ without the rejected transport inference. For the adjoint $a:X\to R_CD$ of any $v$ in the statement, the formula in step 3 gives the fiber map $a_c=v_ci_c$, with $i_c$ as in step 5, so each fiber map is a weak equivalence. The covariant fiberwise criterion of [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation] makes $a$ an equivalence over $N(C)$, consistently with the direct comparison of steps 8–9. Naturality in $X$ and $G$ follows from the actual adjunction formulas, the natural transformation $\alpha$, the derived-adjunction comparison, enriched evaluation, and the natural zigzag in step 9; all these comparisons are natural before localization or are their derived transformations. The base naturality is the normalized equivalence's restriction compatibility in step 1. The arguments allow empty categories and fibers, all simplicial inputs in the adjunction and all strict Kan-valued diagrams in the counit; no projective cofibrancy of $D$ or $G$ was assumed.

source.place: Remark 3.2.5.10 and Lemma 3.2.5.17(1), combined with the explicit counit, fiber and adjunction formulas.
